facility_roles.quote: We propose to use one of the new tunnels to build a neutrino experiment with a fiducial target mass of two kilo-ton for solar neutrino physics

intervals.label: proposed (proposal and letter of intent)
intervals.note: Year precision. The letter of intent was submitted to arXiv on 4 Feb 2016 and published in Chinese Physics C 41, 023002 (2017). A 1-ton prototype was designed (NIM A 855, March 2017); no approval or start of construction of the full detector was found in the sources fetched.
intervals.quote: The Jinping Neutrino Experiment (hereafter referred to as the Jinping experiment) was proposed in 2015

quantity.quote: The proposed experiment will have target mass of 4 kilotons of liquid scintillator or water-based liquid scintillator
with a fiducial mass of 2 kilotons for neutrino-electron scattering events and 3 kilotons for inverse-beta interaction events
which is located 2400 m under the Jinping Mountain in Sichuan, China

name: Jinping Neutrino Experiment
notes: The letter of intent names a "new tunnel" of CJPL-II (then under construction) as the host.

The 1-ton prototype is described by the collaboration in the NIM A 855 design paper; later prototype operation (running since 2017 and moved to CJPL-II according to conference talks seen only in search summaries) is not entered, as no fetchable source states dates.

physics_goals.quote: Jinping Neutrino Experiment (Jinping) is proposed to significantly improve measurements on solar neutrinos and geoneutrinos in China Jinping Laboratory
physics_goals.value: Improve measurements of solar neutrinos (transition from vacuum to matter effect, CNO-cycle neutrinos, solar metallicity) and geoneutrinos at the China Jinping Underground Laboratory

summary.plain: A proposed multi-kiloton liquid-scintillator detector in the deepest underground laboratory in the world, under Jinping Mountain in Sichuan, China, to measure solar neutrinos and geoneutrinos with very low background. A one-tonne prototype has been designed.
summary.technical: Proposed 4 kt (2 kt fiducial for nu-e scattering, 3 kt for IBD) liquid-scintillator or water-based slow-scintillator detector in a new CJPL-II tunnel (~2400 m rock overburden, low reactor background) targeting the vacuum-matter transition of solar neutrino oscillations, CNO neutrinos, the metallicity problem and the separation of U and Th geoneutrinos; a 1-ton prototype (NIM A 855, 81) tests detector components and underground backgrounds.
